entities.summary: Santi Buglioni, by the name of Santi di Michele, was an important Renaissance Italian sculptor, born into a family of artists and the nephew and collaborator of renowned sculptor Benedetto Buglioni. His works, characterized by intricate detail and classical influences, can be found in several prominent churches and cathedrals throughout Italy, including the Basilica of San Lorenzo in Florence. Buglioni's artistic style was heavily influenced by the Mannerist movement, which emphasized dramatic and emotive forms. His collaboration with his uncle led to the creation of several notable sculptures, including the famous "Madonna and Child" for the Oratory of San Matteo in Milan. Buglioni's significance lies in his contribution to the development of Italian Renaissance sculpture, which had a profound impact on the artistic landscape of Europe. Despite his relatively short career, Buglioni's works have endured, with many still admired for their technical skill and emotional depth. The discovery of his lost works in the 20th century has shed new light on the artistic practices of the Mannerist movement and the role of women in Renaissance art.
